newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Allied Domecq upgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Allied Domecq upgraded.

text.p: Allied Domecq Plc shares opened more steadily on Thursday as Credit Lyonnais Laing confirmed it had upgraded the stock to "buy" from "hold".
Allied shares jumped 25-1/2p yesterday in a late flurry of activity, with rumours ranging from a bid from Guinness or Seagram to a possible demerger of the group's operations.
After adding another 3-1/2p shortly after the start, shares slipped back 1p to 481-1/2p by late morning.
Rumours that Allied chief executive Tony Hales may have been meeting with institutions were denied by the company, which said it knew of no reason for the rise in the share price.
Credit Lyonnais upgraded its recommendation in the wake of Allied's disposal of its 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass in August.
It has also adjusted profit expectations to reflect the disposal and forecasts pre-tax profits for 1996 of 578.5 million stg and 619 million stg for the following year.
Credit Lyonnais is the latest of a string of brokerages to have upgraded Allied since the disposal news with HSBC James Capel, Kleinwort Benson and Goldman Sachs all turning more positive last month.
